findings.title: Service receives the job's GITHUB_TOKEN with read access to the whole repo; token can be exfiltrated by the service or leaked via logs
findings.why: The whole point of separating review/post is that the read-only token goes to the service, but this token is still a repo-scoped credential. Passing it in the POST body to the service is by design per the description, but a compromised or malicious REVIEW_AGENTS_URL (set as a secret by repo owner, so lower risk) sees the token. Not a bug per the design; not reporting.

findings.title: Poll loop can exceed 45-minute job timeout because WAIT_SECONDS is checked before sleeping and each request has 60s timeout
findings.why: The review job timeout-minutes is 50 and WAIT_SECONDS is 45 minutes, but each poll call has timeout=60 and sleep is 15s; the check `clock() - start >= WAIT_SECONDS` happens before sleeping, so up to 15+60=75 seconds past WAIT_SECONDS the loop runs, fine within 50m. Not a bug.

findings.title: Superseded status returns 0 from review() but post() returns 1, contradicting the review() docstring
findings.why: review() docstring says 'The job itself fails only on a broken run', but a superseded review is recorded with status 'superseded'. In post(), a superseded result hits the `status in ('skipped','superseded')` branch and returns `0 if outcome.passed else 1`. gate() for status 'superseded' (not 'skipped', not 'done') returns Outcome(False, ...), so post returns 1 (red). A superseded run — superseded by a newer push — should not be red; the newer run's post job decides. This makes the required check red on a superseded run.

findings.title: Walkthrough/summary are upserted only after a successful review; a re-run that skips cannot clear a stale walkthrough, and on failure only summary is replaced
findings.why: When status is 'done' it upserts walkthrough and summary then posts inline comments. When status is not done, it replaces the summary but leaves the walkthrough comment untouched — so a previous successful walkthrough remains visible on top of a failed review. Description says 'A failed review replaces the last summary', which it does, but the walkthrough stale content remains. However not contradicted by description. Not reporting (matches stated behaviour).

findings.title: Race: walkthrough/summary markers upserted before new inline comments are posted; concurrent post jobs (issue_comment run + push run) can double-post inline comments
findings.why: The concurrency group is on the review job only; the post job has no concurrency. Two review/post sequences (e.g. a push and a /review comment) can run post() concurrently. Both read `posted` fingerprints before either writes the inline review, so both POST the same inline comments → duplicate inline comments. Also both upsert summary; last-writer-wins is acceptable but the duplicate inline comments violate D-033's 'not posted yet' guarantee.

findings.title: Base sha used for result but the post job never re-checks the head before posting; a newer push could be posted against a stale head
findings.why: review() checks the head only before submitting. The comment inline POSTs use `commit_id: head` from the result. If a push happens during the 45-minute wait, the review's inline comments are attached to an old commit. The post job does not re-check `head_sha` against the PR's current head, so it can post outdated inline comments and set green/red for a commit that is no longer the head. Description only mentions the review-side check, but the inline posting should also verify; at minimum a stale-but-superseded status handles the service side.

findings.title: issue_comment '/review' path uses event's issue number but fetches PR without verifying it's the PR the comment is on, and does not check the PR head is still current before submitting
findings.why: In the issue_comment branch, `pr = github.ok('GET', f'/pulls/{issue["number"]}')` is fetched but the D-021 head check (`current['head']['sha'] != pr['head']['sha']`) is only in the else branch. A manual /review comment submitted right as a push lands can send the old head to the service and supersede the new push. Root cause: PR head equality check applies only to pull_request_target events.

findings.title: pages() pagination relies on `len(batch) < 100` to stop; an API that returns exactly 100 per page always terminates via a short page, but a fix: no infinite loop here; fine.
findings.why: Not a bug.

findings.title: Inline comments are posted without checking fingerprint idempotency across the reviews endpoint vs individual comments endpoint; on partial batch success the loop re-posts anyway
findings.why: The batch POST /pulls/{number}/reviews may partially succeed? No — GitHub's review creation with multiple comments is atomic: either the review with all comments is created or it 422s. So trying each alone after a batch failure is safe. Not a bug.

findings.title: Rejected-comments section insertion splits on a fixed comment-counts prefix; if the summary from the service has no counts marker, rejected comments are silently dropped
findings.why: `head_part, sep, tail = summary.rpartition('\n<!-- review-agents:counts')`; if sep is empty (no counts line), the code sets `updated = summary` — the rejected inline comments are discarded even though D-033 ③ promises none are lost. The service's summary is not guaranteed to end with a counts comment; the gate reads counts separately from the report object, not from the summary text. Root cause: silent loss of rejected findings when the marker is absent.

findings.title: After posting inline comments, the summary is refetched and upserted, but the rejected section is computed from stale `summary` and then a fresh `_upsert` compares against refreshed comments; if another job changed the summary in between, the rejected section can be applied to the wrong base
findings.why: `refreshed = github.pages(...)` then `_upsert(... refreshed ...)` — but `_upsert` picks the first matching comment from `refreshed` and PATCHes it with `updated` computed from the *old* `summary`, overwriting any concurrent change. Combined with no concurrency on post, two runs can clobber each other's summary edits (e.g. one run's rejected section overwritten by another's).

findings.title: A partial failure posting inline comments (some rejected) still returns green based only on gate; rejected comments only go to summary and do not affect the colour
findings.why: Per description, rejected inline comments go into the summary and colour depends on blocking/complete. This matches the stated contract; not a bug.

findings.title: For a skipped result, post() returns gate outcome; but skipped returns Outcome(True). Then returns 0 if passed else 1 → 0. Fine.
findings.why: Not a bug.

findings.title: upload-artifact step runs even when the review step fails/errors, so a missing result file fails the artifact step and the post job's download fails
findings.why: If review() raises (e.g. env missing → returns 2, or unhandled exception like KeyError on missing event fields, json decode error), the result file may not be written. upload-artifact with a non-existent path fails (default behavior), and download-artifact in post then fails because the artifact does not exist. post's `needs.review.result != 'skipped'` still runs post, but post crashes on read. That does yield red, so the colour is correct; but this is brittle. More importantly, upload-artifact has no `if: always()` — composite action steps: upload-artifact only runs if the previous step succeeded. If review step exits non-zero (it returns 2 for missing secrets), the upload step is skipped, so the artifact is missing. The post job then fails to download → red. Acceptable but the reason is opaque. Also, review() returns 0 even on recorded Failure (writes error result), so upload runs — fine.

findings.title: main() for review uses Path(env['GITHUB_EVENT_PATH']) without guarding; fine. But for post, args.result is read without existence check; if download failed the error is a traceback, not a nice message.
findings.why: Robustness/nit; not a real bug.

findings.title: Ok() treats 3xx as success (code >= 300 fails), correct; but Http follows redirects by default — a 3xx from the service could redirect an HTTPS request to another host, re-sending the signed body to an attacker
findings.why: urllib.request.urlopen follows redirects automatically. The HTTPS-only check is on the initial URL only; a redirected URL (e.g. 307 to http:// or to another host) is followed by urllib without the scheme check, forward-slash the signed body and the GitHub token (in the review POST body) to the redirect target. Root cause: the https check is applied to the requested URL, not to the final response.url. For the GitHub API this is low risk, but for the service (controlled by REVIEW_AGENTS_URL, a secret) a misconfiguration or MITM redirect could leak the body. Real security concern for token leakage. Also redirects for POST resend body.

findings.title: No host allow-list; service URL from secret could be any HTTPS host. By design. Not reporting.

The GitHub token is placed in the JSON body sent to the service (request['token']); if the service URL is misconfigured or the request is redirected, the token leaves GitHub. That's the design per description (review job's token goes to the service). Not reporting.
GitHub.ok error message includes the response message which may echo the token? No. Not a bug.
gate() treats status 'superseded' as failure (No result) — post returns red on a superseded review, which is a normal outcome from concurrency
findings.why: gate() only special-cases 'skipped' and 'done'; 'superseded' falls to `if status != 'done': return Outcome(False, ...)`, producing a red 'No result: superseded'. In post(), the superseded branch is taken early — it calls write_summary and returns `0 if outcome.passed else 1` = 1. So a superseded review (because a newer push cancelled it, per concurrency cancel-in-progress) makes the required check red even though a fresh review is running. This blocks merges incorrectly and is a regression vs. the intent (D-021 says older runs should not supersede newer ones — superseded means the newer one is in flight and will decide). Root cause: superseded is not treated like skipped in the gate.

findings.title: review job's concurrency group uses github.event.pull_request.number || github.event.issue.number for BOTH pull_request_target and issue_comment, so a /review comment cancels an in-flight push review (same group), and cancel-in-progress cancels the actual push review
findings.why: The concurrency group is keyed by PR number only, and cancel-in-progress: true. A comment-triggered run on the same PR shares the group and cancels the running push review. Conversely a push cancels an in-flight manual review. Also, the post job runs after review with `needs: review`; if the review job is cancelled by concurrency, `needs.review.result` is 'cancelled', which is != 'skipped', so post runs — but the review run wrote no artifact (cancelled mid-run), so download-artifact fails in post. That yields red for a cancelled-but-superseded run, blocking merges. Root cause: concurrency cancels the review step before the artifact is written, and post has no guard for `needs.review.result == 'cancelled'`.

findings.title: post job `if: !cancelled() && needs.review.result != 'skipped'` runs when review was cancelled; download-artifact finds no artifact and the post step crashes red — a cancelled (concurrency) run blocks the required check
findings.why: When cancel-in-progress cancels the review job, `needs.review.result` is 'cancelled' and the post job still runs; the result artifact from review was never uploaded, so download-artifact fails and the job is red. A push that supersedes a review therefore makes the superseded run's required check red, blocking merge until a new run finishes — contradicts the design that a newer push makes an older review pointless (D-021). Root cause: no handling of cancelled/skipped artifact.

findings.title: issue_comment trigger runs on every comment but the `review` job `if` doesn't require startsWith on the comment body — it does: `startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '/review')`. Fine. But the `review` job if uses startsWith without trimming leading whitespace, while the script uses lstrip().startswith('/review'). A comment ' /review' would be filtered out by the workflow but accepted by the script if it ran; inconsistent but workflow is stricter. Not a bug.

in the if, github.event.comment.body could be null for non-comment events, but the OR short-circuits via event_name; for pull_request_target the first branch is true. For issue_comment the body exists. Fine.

upload-artifact has no `if: always()` and no `if-no-files-found: warn`; if the review step exits non-zero (missing secrets → returns 2), the artifact is never uploaded; the post job then fails on download — red, but with an unhelpful error instead of the recorded reason
findings.why: When REVIEW_AGENTS_URL/SECRET are missing, main() returns 2 before writing a result file; the review step fails, upload-artifact is skipped (composite steps are sequential; a failed step stops the action). post job runs (needs.review != skipped) and download-artifact fails because the artifact doesn't exist → red with a download error, not the 'secrets must be set' message. The failure reason the reviewer needs is lost. Root cause: no `if: always()` on upload and no graceful handling in post.

findings.title: review() catches Failure but not KeyError/json errors from a malformed service response; a service returning 200 without 'status' or 'id' raises an uncaught exception, the review step crashes, no result file is written, post's download fails
findings.why: In the poll loop, `polled['status']` and in the create `created['id']` are accessed without validating the schema. If the service returns 200 with a body lacking these keys (or a 200 with non-dict? handled), review raises KeyError, not Failure, which propagates out of review(), through main() → traceback → non-zero exit → result file absent → post download fails. Should convert to a recorded Failure/error result. Same for `pr['head']['sha']` from GitHub if the response is unexpected, though GitHub is trusted more.

findings.title: WAIT_SECONDS = 45*60 with job timeout-minutes 50 and each HTTP call timeout 60s: worst case the loop can run past 45 min by up to one poll's request time (60s) plus sleep (15s) = 75s, plus the initial POST and clock; total ~46m15s < 50m, fine. Not a bug.

download-artifact for the result has no fallback; if the artifact is missing (cancelled/failed review), the post step fails before the script runs, so the summary is never updated and the colour comes from the download error
findings.why: Same as above — robustness. Covered under concurrency finding.

findings.title: Retired options are stripped before validation, so a typo like `block_on_criticall` is still a hard error (good), but stripping `block_on_critical` even when the value is garbage (e.g. a nested mapping) hides real config errors
findings.why: Per D-037 the retired option is ignored regardless of value, which the test asserts ('maybe' is ignored). So this matches the intended contract; not a bug. Not reporting.

findings.title: `retired` is only reported from the top-level file; if the config is nested/aliased, fine. But when the rest of the config has an error, _rejected() drops `retired` — so the report won't mention the retired option alongside the error. Acceptable (defaults fallback). Not a bug.

The retired note is always emitted in the scope, but the English text says '{names} ... is no longer used' (singular verb) even for multiple names; if RETIRED_OPTIONS grows to several, grammar is wrong. Style, not a bug.
findings.why: Not reporting (style).

findings.title: gate()/post() wrongly treat 'superseded' as a failure, so a normal superseded review sets the required check red
findings.why: Already reported above duplicated; consolidate into one finding.

findings.title: GitHub.pages on /issues/{n}/comments fetches ALL comments unbounded; a PR with thousands of comments is fully paginated each post, but bounded by reality. Not a bug.
When the review is done but `report.get('comments')` items lack 'body' key or path, KeyError crashes post(); the report schema is not validated
findings.why: `c['body']`, `comment['path']`, `comment['line']`, `comment['body']` are accessed directly. A malformed report from the service (trusted but still remote) crashes post() with a KeyError after possibly having already updated the summary — leaving comments inconsistent and the job red with a traceback rather than a clean message. Schema validation or .get with sensible defaults would be more robust.

findings.title: When report has no 'walksummary'/'summary' key, report['summary'] raises KeyError after walkthrough upsert already happened — partial state
findings.why: Same class as above; report schema not validated.

findings.title: `_ours` picks the FIRST bot comment containing the marker; if there are duplicates (from the no-concurrency race), only one is ever updated and stale duplicates persist forever
findings.why: Because post has no concurrency guard, duplicate walkthrough/summary comments can be created (two concurrent runs both see existing=None). `_ours` only updates the first, leaving permanent duplicates. Root cause: no concurrency control on the post job plus first-match upsert.

findings.title: Inline comments are not deduplicated against comments posted by the per-comment fallback within the same run, but each comment only tried once per endpoint. Fine.
